entries.msgstr: Brooks: I hate Tigers.
Brooks: Sergeant Brooks, 2nd Armored. We ran into a Tiger, too.
Brooks: Now there's two of us.
Brooks: Come with us. The assault of the town has already begun...
Brooks: We need to hurry.
Brooks: Something like that.
Brooks: And is 'Betsy' meant to strike fear into the hearts of our enemy?
Brooks: Enemy at 3 o'clock!
Brooks: Get the Stug first!
Brooks: Let's capture town first. Then we'll see...
Brooks: There's no time to waste. Let's move.
Brooks: Wake up! We're moving forward.
Brooks: Keep up, Sherman.
Brooks: They need us in town - come on.
Brooks: Forward, forward, forward!
Brooks: Self-propelled gun at 12 o'clock. Destroy it pronto!
Brooks: Got 'em! Nice job, Sherman.
Brooks: Platoon - new enemy!
Brooks: Move to the center. Stay focused.
Brooks: Well done. Now let's clear the last square. Forward!
Brooks: Attention! More enemies than we expected!
Brooks: New enemy group! Don't let them flank you, Lucky!
Brooks: Thanks for the help. We won this fight, but we have more battles ahead.
Brooks: Now, now, Betsy.
Brooks: The assault's already begun - we need to hurry.
Brooks: In honor of your grandfather?
Brooks: Sherman, follow us. Let's not waste any more time.
Brooks: It sounds too German.
Brooks: Enemy at 2 o'clock! Fire at will!
Brooks: Enemy at 12 o'clock! Fire at will!
Brooks: Destroyed. Let's move to town.
Brooks: It instills fear... But it's not very original.
Brooks: Let's roll, let's roll! Our allies are waiting for us.
Brooks: Two opponents at 12 o'clock. Fire!
Brooks: Eyes peeled, Commander! Let's drive around from the right.
Brooks: There's a German Panzer. Fire AP shells!
Brooks: Let's move. Everybody, stay alert. Air force is hitting the town.
Brooks: But there'll still be plenty of enemy vehicles.
Brooks: Don't get too excited, MacLeod. This is...
Brooks: Damnit! Here's our first assault squad. Was it a Tiger?
Brooks: And here they come!
Brooks: Stay focused, MacLeod!
Brooks: A VK on the other bank! Fire at will!
Brooks: That's the first I'm hearing you begging for a target.
Brooks: The bridge is blocked. We need to go around.
Brooks: Optimism is good preparation for a mission. There's a ford nearby.
Brooks: You're a damn fortune teller. How'd you do that?
Brooks: Then why didn't you warn us? That was the enemy.
Brooks: Enemy at 12 o'clock!
Brooks: Save your shells, Lucky! Don't shoot willy-nilly; use the optics.
Brooks: Let's finish 'em off and move on.
Brooks: We need to catch up with the second assault squad.
Brooks: Just don't lose your head. A Tiger's a Tiger.
Brooks: They're incredibly dangerous.
Brooks: Harping on your medal again! Are you only here for decorations?
Brooks: Good news: We caught up with the second group.
Brooks: Damnit! Flank it! Flank it!
Brooks: Damnit! Fire like you mean it!
Brooks: Platoon, your attention: All allied groups have been destroyed.
Brooks: We're alone now. We need to complete the mission. Let's roll.
Brooks: Enemy! 12 o'clock!
Brooks: I don't think these were the last.
Brooks: Recon suggested we'd see more than Tigers.
Brooks: Holy... That's not a Panther. That's a King Tiger.
Brooks: You should get a medal for that, for sure.
Brooks: We can't penetrate it from the front. Let's flank it.
Brooks: Move! Don't let 'em aim!
Brooks: Damnit! My track's hit. I'm immobilized!
MacLeod: But they burn so nicely.
MacLeod: That one was burning nicely, too.
MacLeod: Hey, Sergeant Brooks - why 'Thunderbolt'?
MacLeod: To strike fear into the hearts of our enemy with nought but a name?
MacLeod: Hm... My Firefly needs a name, too. I'll call her 'Betsy'.
MacLeod: It's in honor of my nana. I was well afraid of her...
MacLeod: Hey, Sherman, ye awake? Just in time!
MacLeod: Ye vermin!
MacLeod: Nice shot, Sherman! Glad to see you're back on yer feet!
MacLeod: Two more to my score! Sergeant Brooks, where's my medal?
MacLeod: Typical...
MacLeod: Let's roll, Sherman.
MacLeod: Sherman, wake up.
MacLeod: Don't just stand there. Drive!
MacLeod: Has yer tank stalled again or what?
MacLeod: Let's get a move on, else we'll miss the show!
MacLeod: Argh, ye piece of... You'll answer for that!
MacLeod: Use the optics, Lucky!
MacLeod: Ah! It just came out. Guess I'll be calling ye Lucky!
MacLeod: All good, Lucky. We were certainly missing yer style around here.
MacLeod: Wow! There's plenty for everyone.
MacLeod: Care for a wee bit o' competition, Lucky?
MacLeod: Go on, burn 'em down!
MacLeod: What a flame!
MacLeod: That was hot! You've got my respect.
MacLeod: It's been some time since I saw something like this!
MacLeod: Oy, Sergeant Brooks, how about that medal?
MacLeod: Ha!
MacLeod: Let's come up with a name for the Sherman, as well.
MacLeod: Ha! His name was Ruaraidh.
MacLeod: That'll certainly scare the enemy.
MacLeod: But I'm afraid ye won't be able to spell it!
MacLeod: Alright, Sherman, let's go. The show's already started!
MacLeod: Drive around, Sherman.
MacLeod: If ye catch it, you'll lose speed and become an easy target.
MacLeod: Maybe Battlewagon? How's about that name?
MacLeod: Here we go! Let's make some extra holes in that there clunker!
MacLeod: What about Death Machine?
MacLeod: Says Thunderbolt!
MacLeod: Our lads ken what they're doing! What a spectacular fire show!
MacLeod: Fire, Death Machine, fire!
MacLeod: We need a shorter name.
MacLeod: C'mon! Turn yer turret! Fry those rust buckets!
MacLeod: Holy smokes! That was a close call.
MacLeod: Ye ain't getting away from us! Let's chase 'em...
MacLeod: Reaper? How about Reaper?
MacLeod: Let the hunt begin!
MacLeod: So, Lucky, looks like this'll be the very day when MacLeod snags the title of 'Tiger Hunter' from ye!
MacLeod: No. Different hole sizes. Those were medium tanks.
MacLeod: Pfft... Small game. Nothing interesting.
MacLeod: Sir, yes sir! Keep up, Lucky!
MacLeod: That wasnae smart of 'em. With our optics, they're sitting ducks.
MacLeod: Here comes the second. Hey, Lucky - leave me at least one, will ye?
MacLeod: Damn! Did I say that out loud?
MacLeod: Be more optimistic, Sergeant! There'll be a pass now.
MacLeod: I've got good eyes. Saw the plane.
MacLeod: Aye?! Thought it was ours.
MacLeod: It's like we're at a shooting range. What're they thinking?
MacLeod: I think they'll be the ones playing catch-up.
MacLeod: They took quite the detour. Through your ford.
MacLeod: Those Tigers have our names on 'em.
MacLeod: And that's good.
MacLeod: How many do I need to blast to finally earn my medal?
MacLeod: Dinnae care 'bout it one bit.
MacLeod: I just want to send it to my maw - to make her happy, you know?
MacLeod: She'll show it off to all our neighbors. And she'll be proud of me.
MacLeod: At last.
MacLeod: That is one sturdy mongrel.
MacLeod: Aim at the weak spots, Lucky! The sides and rear!
MacLeod: This one burns nicely!
MacLeod: That's a sturdy mongrel! Look for its weak spots, Lucky.
MacLeod: Aim at its belly - it's always thin under the frontal armor.
MacLeod: That's a sturdy mongrel! Look for its weak spots, Lucky!
MacLeod: Aim at its belly - it's always thin under the frontal armor!
MacLeod: Aim at the cupolas - they're hard to hit but easy to penetrate.
MacLeod: Remember to move, Lucky. Or they'll hit ye in yer weak spots.
MacLeod: Or ye can hide yer hull behind tank wrecks.
MacLeod: They winnae get ye at all that way - you've got a strong turret.
MacLeod: Those recon guys... Probably know nothing.
MacLeod: Who else can there be? Panthers?
MacLeod: Havnae seen this one before.
MacLeod: Aye, finally!
MacLeod: Lucky! Sides! Rear! Hit the weak spots!
MacLeod: No chance this numpty can keep up with us Shermans.
MacLeod: Lucky, go get 'em - quick!
MacLeod: Brooks! Damn it, Brooks, say something!
MacLeod: Flank 'em! Hit their weak spots!
MacLeod: Lucky, get their sides and rear!
MacLeod: The turret's only sturdy from the front. Keep moving!
MacLeod: That's it.
MacLeod: They're burning. Burning nicely.
MacLeod: The Tiger Hunter: It's officially your title, mate.
Brooks: HQ here. Sergeant Brooks to Tiger Hunters.
Brooks: The city and its outskirts are riddled with mines. Tread carefully.
Brooks: I'm glad to hear that, MacLeod.
Brooks: But stay sharp out there. Expect massive minefields along the way.
Brooks: Give what a good rub?
Brooks: What makes you think Lucky's also got a ritual?
Brooks: Don't get overconfident now. Aim at the same target. Stay together.
Brooks: Old man? Really?
Brooks: I'm only six years your senior, MacLeod.
Brooks: Perhaps they're just being polite, letting you do all the talking, MacLeod!
Brooks: MacLeod, give me a status report.
Brooks: Same old MacLeod.
Brooks: You've got Lucky. He brings luck better than any charm.
Brooks: Find an alternate route, boys!
Brooks: Heads up, Hunters.
Brooks: Allied bombers are approaching your position. Be cautious.
Brooks: Keep your distance from those enemy tanks.
Brooks: Are you ok?
Brooks: No advice, MacLeod. But we've got air support. Patching in the pilot now.
Brooks: Stay on target, MacLeod. We've got one last square to clear.
Brooks: You can discuss your superstitions over a cup of tea later.
Brooks: Whatever you say.
Brooks: Don’t be dumb, I don’t need lucky charms.
Brooks: Planning and Strategy, McLeod, Planning and Strategy.
Brooks: A desk what?
Brooks: Damn, intel didn't report this…
Brooks: We're doing the best we can.
Brooks: I got a report that Eagle One is alive. Good job, lads.
Brooks: You're right, MacLeod, sometimes we do need those lucky charms.
Brooks: And yeah, I do have one. A tintinnabulum with a fascinus.
Brooks: (laughing)
Brooks: Lucky, time to roll. We're not here for sightseeing.
Brooks: Forward, Lucky! Every second counts in this fight.
Brooks: Lucky, we've got a mission to complete. Let's get moving.
Brooks: Betsy really said that?
Brooks: Time's against us. No heroics now.
Brooks: Always pinch the enemy in a vice if you can. Make them squirm and hit their sides.
Brooks: Sending reinforcements your way. Hang tight.
Brooks: Backup's on the way. Should be there shortly.
Brooks: New allied tanks are en route.
Brooks: Back on track, commander. Keep your head down and push forward.
Brooks: Handle this tank with care. We're running low on reserves.
Brooks: You've got another shot at this. Make it count.
Brooks: HQ here, Sergeant Brooks speaking.
Brooks: No, they're not.
Brooks: I hope.
Brooks: No. Something big and heavy. The allies have made several attempts already.
Brooks: Sent a few tank platoons. None came back.
Brooks: No, intel is reporting that our target is still in the city.
Brooks: Hold off! Now's not the time for risks! You have a different mission to focus on.
Brooks: I suggest using the ace up your sleeve.
Brooks: HQ to Storm Petrel, come in.
Brooks: Target is a King Tiger on the bridge at grid C3.
Brooks: Hold off, MacLeod. The stakes are too high.
Brooks: Work together. Immobilize the Tiger. Storm Petrel will make another pass.
Brooks: Immobilize the Tiger. Storm Petrel will make another pass.
Brooks: We don't have clear information, MacLeod.
Brooks: Something experimental. A prototype. And a good one at that.
Brooks: MacLeod, you don't have time for this. It's not your problem.
Brooks: Bypass it through the side streets. And give Bennett the coordinates.
Brooks: Storm Petrel.
Brooks: Typ 205.
Brooks: Why "Little Mouse"?
Brooks: That is intel. They were supposed to be back at base by now.
Brooks: Sorry, MacLeod. Slipped out, I suppose.
Brooks: I might, but arranging that will take some time.
Brooks: It was a covert op.
Brooks: But you decided you wanted to take care of that Jagdtiger yourself.
Brooks: They got stuck in frontal assaults.
Brooks: The bombers are lining up on their run now. Get ready for some fireworks.
Brooks: Since when did you start grumbling, MacLeod?
Brooks: Who said those were his first Tigers? Why do you think I brought him on this mission?
Brooks: You make a good team, MacLeod.
Brooks: Damn! Lucky, be careful and…good luck!
Brooks: Reinforcements are en route to your position.
Brooks: The allied tanks you saved. MacLeod, your efforts weren't in vain.
Brooks: A new group of allies has arrived.
Brooks: Hopefully it'll be easier to take down this Little Mouse with their help.
Brooks: But remember, the final shot needs to be ours.
Brooks: It's got to be our trophy. Lucky, Bennett, don't let us down.
Brooks: Great job, guys. Sending a team for evac.
Brooks: MacLeod, we need to get you and the Mouse out. It's crucial it falls into our hands.
Brooks: Consider your medals in the bag.
Brooks: What do you want then, MacLeod? A new rank?
MacLeod: Alright, gents, it's time to roll out and clear this town!
MacLeod: Brooks?! Sergeant Brooks?! That's good news! We're in safe hands!
MacLeod: Sir, yes sir!
MacLeod: Lads! Give those lucky coins of yours a good rub before firing the first shot!
MacLeod: What? I’m not superstitious, it's just a tradition!
MacLeod: Ah, here come our lovebirds.
MacLeod: First round of Scotch "tea" is on me for whoever destroys the most!
MacLeod: Let's show 'em how we do it, Lucky!
MacLeod: Bit too quiet for my liking. Where's the challenge?
MacLeod: Anyway...Lucky, spill the beans—what's your lucky ritual?
MacLeod: We all have our little tricks for good luck, right, Lucky?
MacLeod: Maybe a dance? A quick jig before you jump into the fray?
MacLeod: Ah, now we're talking! These chaps look like they've got some fight in them.
MacLeod: Wise words, old man Brooks. Lucky, lend me a hand with this one, will ya?
MacLeod: I'll keep the beast busy, and you sneak around on its right.
MacLeod: Let's give 'em a proper surprise, eh?
MacLeod: This one's a tough nut to crack, Lucky! Rip it apart!
MacLeod: Don't let that one slip away! He'll muck up our whole surprise!
MacLeod: Done and dusted!
MacLeod: Just a bit of friendly banter with all due respect, “si-i-i-ir”!
MacLeod: Alright, alright, I know.
MacLeod: Lads, why are you so tight-lipped today?
MacLeod: Ha!
MacLeod: Seems like we've kicked over a few anthills in this mess.
MacLeod: Remember to tuck your hull behind those mounds or burnt enemies, Lucky.
MacLeod: Just give 'em a peek at your turret—that's the toughest bit of your tank.
MacLeod: Right, this one's a serious contender, no messing about.
MacLeod: We can't take him head-on, so stick to the plan.
MacLeod: I'll grab his attention, and you sneak around for the flank. But watch yourself, Lucky.
MacLeod: If it turns its sights on you, don't try playing the hero—duck out.
MacLeod: Its gun'll slice through our Shermans like butter.
MacLeod: Just keep it busy, and I'll nip in to give it a bite from behind.
MacLeod: Phew, that was a tough one!
MacLeod: Haven't run into a single Tiger yet. We need them to find out who's the best!
MacLeod: Old! Ha!
MacLeod: Whoa, hold it, lads!
MacLeod: Mines. And here you were laughing about lucky charms, Brooks.
MacLeod: We need all the luck we can get here!
MacLeod: Hey, Lucky! Found us a different route. Let's roll.
MacLeod: What would you do without good ol' MacLeod!
MacLeod: You'd be sitting here till nightfall! Ha!
MacLeod: Oh! You found a detour! Brilliant!
MacLeod: I was beginning to think we'd be stuck here waiting for the engineers till evening.
MacLeod: Look at that, Lucky! Two Tigers! Our competition's back on track.
MacLeod: But this street's too tight. Cracking a Tiger's frontal armor is no easy feat.
MacLeod: Nice! Just you wait, we're about to witness some fine work.
MacLeod: Our boys in the sky will take out those steel beasts with surgical precision.
MacLeod: Whoa, what was that?! It was too loud!
MacLeod: Whoa, what was that?!
MacLeod: Yeah, we're intact, but I've dropped my lucky coin!
MacLeod: And I can't see a few buildings that used to be here.
MacLeod: Lucky! Look, there's the second Tiger, still kicking.
MacLeod: Let's use this new gap to our advantage. Squeeze it from both sides.
MacLeod: Good shot! That's another Tiger chalked up to our tally!
MacLeod: Well, blow me down! More Tigers! What did we do to deserve all these gifts?
MacLeod: Damn, it's still crowded here. Brooks, any advice?
MacLeod: I like this guy's style! Lucky, let's stick to our playbook. Use this new passage.
MacLeod: I'll press from the front, and you sneak around the side.
MacLeod: Let's make this rascal dance like it's on a hot skillet.
MacLeod: Wait till we've both reloaded so he doesn't know which side the hit's coming from.
MacLeod: They might look tough from the front. But their sides and back are soft and juicy!
MacLeod: There must be something that brings you luck, Lucky. Maybe you've got…
MacLeod: Traditions, Brooks. Not superstitions.
MacLeod: Alright, it's about time we wrap up this grand tour. Eagle One, do you read?
MacLeod: Give us the bird's-eye view—how many adoring fans do we still have loitering in the square?
MacLeod: I must say, I like this lad!
MacLeod: Pity he's not in the tank business. We could've used a chap like him in our crew.
MacLeod: Well then, that's one who's flown his last.
MacLeod: Eagle One, be careful up there, enemy fighters are dropping out of the sky.
MacLeod: Mines! I hate mines. Find a detour, Lucky. I'll draw their attention.
MacLeod: Let's say Lucky was born under a lucky star.
MacLeod: But what about you, Brooks? Got your own lucky charm?
MacLeod: A horseshoe in your pocket? Maybe a tintinnabulum with a fascinus?
MacLeod: Hang on. Did I guess it right?
MacLeod: Look, lads, that's how legends do it!
MacLeod: If it weren't for his injury, Brooks would be here with us too!
MacLeod: The three of us together... Ah, well, can't be helped. Now he's a desk...
MacLeod: A desk legend, sir!
MacLeod: Bloody hell! The last thing we need now is an SPG joining the party.
MacLeod: Don't just sit there, Lucky—move! Let's make them risk hitting their own.
MacLeod: Brooks, where did these uninvited guests come from?
MacLeod: There was no mention of them in the briefing.
MacLeod: Oh, my beloved intel…always sticking to their traditions.
MacLeod: Eagle One, how many can you take off our hands?
MacLeod: Eagle One, over! Eagle One! Damn!
MacLeod: Brooks, tell me you have some fighters to help them out!
MacLeod: Lucky, can you see him? Come on, Eagle One, you can shake them off. Bloody hell!
MacLeod: Let's wrap this up here, Lucky. We'll squeeze them from both sides. No niceties.
MacLeod: Looks like we've got a bit more company than anticipated.
MacLeod: Focusing on the same target. We'll pick them off one by one, Lucky.
MacLeod: And for pudding, we'll serve up a nice slice of that artillery!
MacLeod: Phew...that was tough. Oh, look at this! I've found my lucky coin!
MacLeod: Hold on. What?! Seriously? I've got to see this!
MacLeod: Move out, Lucky, or our tea will be as cold and nasty as a Scottish winter.
MacLeod: Let's get rolling, Lucky! Those Tigers aren't going to knock themselves out!
MacLeod: No mines here, Lucky. Time to move.
MacLeod: Lucky, we're not here for a picnic. Let's go!
MacLeod: Don't just stand there, Lucky. Arty never sleeps.
MacLeod: Lucky, let's find a way around these mines.
MacLeod: Don't just sit there, Lucky. Scout out an alternate route.
MacLeod: Staring at those mines won't make them disappear, Lucky.
MacLeod: Let's find ourselves a detour.
MacLeod: As my nana used to say, "Always flank your foe and pummel their sides with armor-piercing rounds."
MacLeod: Well, more or less.
MacLeod: Remember: Squeeze the enemy from both sides, and they'll always expose a weak spot to one of us.
MacLeod: Let's box them in, flank on both sides.
MacLeod: That way, they're bound to expose a vulnerable spot.
MacLeod: Let's do it by the book: Attack from both sides, and one of us is bound to get a juicy slice of that thin side armor!
MacLeod: Watch your step, Lucky!
MacLeod: Beware the mines!
MacLeod: Hold up! These mines aren't exactly fond of our tanks!
MacLeod: Mines. I hate mines.
MacLeod: Careful! The mines round here have a nasty temper.
MacLeod: Mines ahead! Better find another way.
MacLeod: Lucky! That was quite the bang! You alright there?
MacLeod: Hold on! Where are you off to in such a hurry?
MacLeod: Fix your tracks and reverse out of there!
MacLeod: Lucky, if you wanted to dig a hole, there are easier ways, you know!
MacLeod: Hard lines, Lucky. These mines are a sneaky lot.
MacLeod: Well, that's one way to find a mine. Not the best, but it works.
MacLeod: Shake it off, Lucky. We've all danced with a mine or two.
MacLeod: Watch it, Lucky! The next mine might be your last.
MacLeod: Seems you've got a fondness for fixing tracks, Lucky.
MacLeod: What?! Again? Where's this love for mines coming from, Lucky?
MacLeod: Damn, we just lost one of our tanks.
MacLeod: Blast it! There goes another one of ours!
MacLeod: Lost an allied tank. We'll need to redouble our efforts now.
MacLeod: My tank's destroyed. Be back in a jiffy with a new one! Don't miss me too much.
MacLeod: Ah, blast it! That was my favorite tank. Alright, round two coming up soon!
MacLeod: I’m hit. Don’t worry, I’ll be back with another—hope they have my favorite color.
MacLeod: Well, that’s just great. Another tank down. Give me a minute, I’ll be back soon.
MacLeod: Looks like I’m in the market for a new tank again.
MacLeod: Hold tight, I’ll be back faster than you can say "Where's MacLeod?"
MacLeod: Back in the saddle, eh? Show 'em what you're made of!
MacLeod: Rise and shine, time for round two! You've got this.
MacLeod: We're not running a tank dealership here. Take care of this one.
MacLeod: Ha! There's no stopping you, is there? Back for more, I see!
MacLeod: Tiger Hunters at the rendezvous point.
MacLeod: Brooks, if I can call you that on the air, you there?
MacLeod: Why so formal, Brooks? We all know it's you.
MacLeod: Now you tell me, do our allies know we're in the city?
MacLeod: They're not going to fire at us, are they?
MacLeod: Why doesn't that answer fill me with confidence?
MacLeod: What are we looking for, Brooks? Not this small fry, surely?
MacLeod: Someone made it back. I see an allied tank. Have we missed the action?
MacLeod: Ah, intel...
MacLeod: Damn! We've got another one here.
MacLeod: It's...oh, Brooks, it's that beast again. The King Tiger.
MacLeod: Lucky, we know what to do. Ready?
MacLeod: What do you suggest? Run away? Leave it here?
MacLeod: Nice try, but looks like...
MacLeod: Let's give old man Brooks something to smile about, Lucky.
MacLeod: Aim for the front or rear drive wheel. Easiest way to track an enemy.
MacLeod: Aim for the front or rear drive wheel. Easiest way to track an enemy.
MacLeod: Keep firing. Sooner or later, that track will come off.
MacLeod: And this carriage will turn into a pumpkin.
MacLeod: Keep firing. Sooner or later, that track will come off.
MacLeod: That's the way! Great shot. Seagull, your move.
MacLeod: You sound like my old biology teacher. Mrs. McFuddlebrains.
MacLeod: Lucky, let's move out before another King Kitty shows up.
MacLeod: Brooks, give us a clue, what are we looking for?
MacLeod: Something bigger than a King Tiger? An Emperor?
MacLeod: I see Allied tanks up ahead. As usual, they're mobbing and trying to push through.
MacLeod: They won't get past the Jagdtiger like that. Lucky, are we counting Jagdtigers?
MacLeod: Brooks, seems like you've been in HQ too long.
MacLeod: I get it, you have reports to write. But our allies need help out here.
MacLeod: Bennett?
MacLeod: That's more like it. Lucky, let's help our winged friend score a few points!
MacLeod: Let's make short work of these tin cans. Need to reach that Jagdtiger quickly.
MacLeod: If we run into tougher nuts, aim for the drive wheels.
MacLeod: Give our 'seabird' a bit of target practice.
MacLeod: Aim for the drive wheels. Give our 'seabird' a bit of target practice.
MacLeod: What's this prototype called anyway?
MacLeod: Got a code name? Or should I come up with one myself?
MacLeod: Boring name. I'll call it...the Little Mouse.
MacLeod: If I were a German engineer, I'd name it that just for fun.
MacLeod: How many of you are there? I'm running late for my date with the Jagdtiger.
MacLeod: Lucky, let's pick up the pace. It's not gentlemanly to keep a lady waiting.
MacLeod: Whoa! And who might you be?
MacLeod: Brooks! Why didn't you warn us about friendly units here?
MacLeod: Don't tell me intel dropped the ball again!
MacLeod: So this is what our intel looks like.
MacLeod: Come with us, it's not wise to leave the city alone.
MacLeod: God. You're as chatty as the guys from the last op.
MacLeod: Alright, let's move, we're late for a meeting.
MacLeod: Seagull!
MacLeod: I mean Storm Petrel! We've found you a juicy target. Hard to miss this one.
MacLeod: Lucky, aim for the drive wheel!
MacLeod: Lucky, aim for the drive wheel!
MacLeod: Copy that. Soon we'll have a tar...wait. What?!
MacLeod: Oh...Brooks, you b... That was our little secret!
MacLeod: Yeah, of course. Old age, I understand.
MacLeod: We're close now, fellas. Your guardian angels are about to take care of your curse.
MacLeod: What's the matter now?
MacLeod: Brooks, you wouldn't happen to have another ace up your sleeve, something the size of a bomber, would you?
